rules.between:
Success: the target's reference point ends within 4.44 cm of the straight line through the two referents' reference points, and closer to each referent's reference point than those two are to each other (exact midpoint not required). An object's reference point is the centre of the rectangle that bounds it as seen from above (its top-down outline's bounding box), to within about a millimetre for most objects and up to about 3 cm for a few long ones. Only that point of the target is judged against the line, not where the rest of the object lies. The target must also have moved at least 2.54 cm, and the robot must not be touching it. Failures: (1) any object other than the target, both referents included, moved more than 2.54 cm from its start; (2) the target, or any object held in the gripper, touching any other object (the table, the bin and the robot do not count) for more than 5 s without a break. Only the target may be grasped or moved on purpose; touching other objects with the robot is not scored by itself, but it is how they get displaced, so avoid it. How judging works: positions and displacements are measured in the tabletop plane (height ignored) from where each object and the bin rest when you take control. The robot 'touches' an object when any robot link presses on it with more than 0.05 N. Every success condition must hold continuously for 5 s of simulated time; any break restarts that count. Every failure condition ends the episode once it has held continuously for 5 s (undoing it sooner, e.g. putting a nudged object back, avoids the failure). If the time limit arrives while success is being confirmed, the episode is extended until the confirmation finishes; if success breaks during that extension, the episode fails.
Shared task guidance:
Be VERY slow and patient during spatial placement. The held object, gripper and arm must avoid both referents/blockers and all other non-target objects. Carry above obstacles, descend above the intended position, and inspect fresh images between small moves. Below a grasp-point height of 0.10 m, lower by at most 1 cm per command before looking again. Stop with the object just clear of the table, release gently, then withdraw vertically before moving sideways. Check the released placement and correct it carefully if time allows. Aim the target's reference point onto the straight line through the referents' centers, near the midpoint: zero offset, not merely within tolerance. Orient long objects so both ends remain clear of both referents. After release, re-estimate all three positions and the perpendicular offset; correct an offset over about 1 cm if time allows without contact. Judge grasp acquisition, clearance and placement from fresh camera images. A closed jaw alone does not prove a grasp. Keep the gripper commanded closed while carrying; release deliberately. Leave enough simulated time for the required five-second success confirmation. Do not claim success solely because a motion command returned successfully.

rules.move:
Directions are in the robot's frame: left = +x, right = -x, forward = -y (away from the robot base), backward = +y (toward the base). At the start of the episode the benchmark picks a blocker: the NEAREST other object ahead of the target in that direction whose outline overlaps at least 10% of the target's sideways extent; it stays the blocker for the whole episode. Success with a blocker: the gap from the target's leading edge to the blocker's facing edge, measured along the direction, ends at most 5.08 cm (no minimum gap, and ending past that edge is allowed, but the target resting against the blocker is contact, failure 4 below); moving the target well along the direction is not enough if it stops further than that from the blocker. Success with no blocker: the middle of the target's outline progresses at least 5.08 cm in the direction. In both cases the middle of its outline must be within 5.08 cm sideways of the straight path from its start, the target must have moved at least 2.54 cm in total, and the robot must not be touching it. Failures: (1) the blocker's facing edge moved more than 1.27 cm along the direction; (2) any object other than the target moved more than 2.54 cm from its start; (3) the target's sideways deviation over 5.08 cm; (4) the target, or any object held in the gripper, touching any other object (the table, the bin and the robot do not count; the blocker does) for more than 5 s without a break. Only the target may be grasped or moved on purpose; touching other objects with the robot is not scored by itself, but it is how they get displaced, so avoid it. How judging works: positions and displacements are measured in the tabletop plane (height ignored) from where each object and the bin rest when you take control. The robot 'touches' an object when any robot link presses on it with more than 0.05 N. Every success condition must hold continuously for 5 s of simulated time; any break restarts that count. Every failure condition ends the episode once it has held continuously for 5 s (undoing it sooner, e.g. putting a nudged object back, avoids the failure). If the time limit arrives while success is being confirmed, the episode is extended until the confirmation finishes; if success breaks during that extension, the episode fails.

Be VERY slow and patient during spatial placement. The held object, gripper and arm must avoid both referents/blockers and all other non-target objects. Find the blocker specified by the task rules. Target a 1-2 cm gap from the leading edge of the target to the facing edge of the blocker along the move direction, without contact. Keep the target centered on its straight path. Check edge gaps before and after release. rules.bin:
Success: every object on the table ends with its reference point inside the plastic bin's footprint seen from above (height does not matter), with the robot touching none of the objects. An object's reference point is the centre of the rectangle that bounds it as seen from above (its top-down outline's bounding box), to within about a millimetre for most objects and up to about 3 cm for a few long ones. Failure: the bin moved more than 1.27 cm from its start (the robot may brush the bin but must not shift it, directly or by pushing an object into it). In this task every object is a target, so objects may touch each other and other objects may be moved while you work; only the bin's position is limited. How judging works: positions and displacements are measured in the tabletop plane (height ignored) from where each object and the bin rest when you take control. The robot 'touches' an object when any robot link presses on it with more than 0.05 N. Every success condition must hold continuously for 5 s of simulated time; any break restarts that count. Every failure condition ends the episode once it has held continuously for 5 s (undoing it sooner, e.g. putting a nudged object back, avoids the failure). If the time limit arrives while success is being confirmed, the episode is extended until the confirmation finishes; if success breaks during that extension, the episode fails.
Shared task guidance:
Grasp and place every object in the bin. Verify acquisition and release using both views. Avoid shifting the bin. Once all objects are in, release and withdraw the arm so it contacts no object. Judge grasp acquisition, clearance and placement from fresh camera images. A closed jaw alone does not prove a grasp. Keep the gripper commanded closed while carrying; release deliberately. Leave enough simulated time for the required five-second success confirmation. Do not claim success solely because a motion command returned successfully.
